waves.title: The Waves
waves.author: Virginia Woolf
waves.why: Six friends' inner lives in poetic, stream-of-consciousness prose; beautiful but demanding, loved by readers of experimental fiction.

exhalation.title: Exhalation
exhalation.author: Ted Chiang
exhalation.why: Ted Chiang's thoughtful short science fiction about time, free will and consciousness, picked as a favourite story collection.

shuggie bain.title: Shuggie Bain
shuggie bain.author: Douglas Stuart
shuggie bain.why: A boy in 1980s Glasgow cares for his alcoholic mother; devastating and beautifully written.

kaiju preservation society.title: The Kaiju Preservation Society
kaiju preservation society.author: John Scalzi
kaiju preservation society.why: A breezy adventure about people protecting giant monsters on a parallel Earth; just fun, with quick, witty writing.

jude the obscure.title: Jude the Obscure
jude the obscure.author: Thomas Hardy
jude the obscure.why: A stonemason's doomed struggle against class and marriage in Victorian England, grim and moving.

of human bondage.title: Of Human Bondage
of human bondage.author: William Somerset Maugham
of human bondage.why: A long coming-of-age story of an orphan with a club foot, called one of the best books by readers.

careless people.title: Careless People
careless people.author: Sarah Wynn-Williams
careless people.why: An insider's account of working at Facebook, interesting and eye-opening for many readers.

gnomon.title: Gnomon
gnomon.author: Nick Harkaway
gnomon.why: A near-future surveillance state and an interrogation across layered stories; complex but rewarding for fans of puzzle plots.

death of the author.title: Death of the Author
death of the author.author: Nnedi Okorafor
death of the author.why: A novel where a writer's life and her creations intertwine; a recent release that readers enjoyed.

alias grace.title: alias Grace
alias grace.author: Margaret Atwood
alias grace.why: A fictional take on a real convicted murderess, told through her memory; Atwood's literary mystery.

riddley walker.title: Riddley Walker
riddley walker.author: Russell Hoban
riddley walker.why: A boy narrates a post-nuclear England in invented broken English; underrated, odd and moving.

solenoid.title: Solenoid
solenoid.author: Mircea Cărtărescu
solenoid.why: A Romanian teacher's mundane life collides with surreal visions in a huge, brilliant dreamlike novel.

invisible monsters.title: Invisible Monsters
invisible monsters.author: Chuck Palahniuk
invisible monsters.why: A disfigured model's twisted road trip in this wild, transgressive novel.

bury our bones in the midnight soil.title: Bury Our Bones in the Midnight Soil
bury our bones in the midnight soil.author: V. E. Schwab
bury our bones in the midnight soil.why: Not a clear recommendation of this book.

lady tans circle of women.title: Lady Tan's Circle of Women
lady tans circle of women.author: Lisa See
lady tans circle of women.why: A woman physician in Ming-dynasty China fights for her place; engrossing historical fiction on women's lives.

mary.title: Mary
mary.author: Nat Cassidy
mary.why: Not a clear recommendation of this book.

stiff.title: Stiff
stiff.author: Mary Roach
stiff.why: A funny, fascinating tour of what happens to human bodies after death, praised as laugh-out-loud science writing.

vita nostra.title: Vita Nostra
vita nostra.author: Marina and Sergey Dyachenko
vita nostra.why: A girl enters a strange institute where reality bends and she is slowly transformed; readers re-read it yearly.

down the drain.title: Down the Drain
down the drain.author: Julia Fox
down the drain.why: A celebrity memoir read cover to cover in one day by fans who found it gripping.

under the whispering door.title: Under the Whispering Door
under the whispering door.author: T. J. Klune
under the whispering door.why: A cozy afterlife tale about a man who runs a tea shop for the dead; warm and good for grief.

outlander.title: Outlander
outlander.author: Diana Gabaldon
outlander.why: A WWII nurse is thrown back to 18th-century Scotland; a huge romantic saga with devoted fans.

forever.title: Forever
forever.author: Pete Hamill
forever.why: An Irish man gains immortality as long as he stays in New York, tracing the city's history.

gormenghast.title: Gormenghast
gormenghast.author: Mervyn Peake
gormenghast.why: A vast crumbling castle and its rigid inhabitants, written in rich, long sentences; a gothic classic of fantasy.

ringworld.title: Ringworld
ringworld.author: Larry Niven
ringworld.why: Explorers visit an enormous artificial ring with a strange civilisation; a hard-SF classic of big ideas.

last letter.title: The Last Letter
last letter.author: Rebecca Yarros
last letter.why: A wartime love story told in letters; an ugly-cry read for those who like emotional romance.

neverending story.title: The Neverending Story
neverending story.author: Michael Ende
neverending story.why: A boy finds a book that takes him to a magical world, much richer than the film; a child's fantasy classic.

eyre affair.title: The Eyre Affair
eyre affair.author: Jasper Fforde
eyre affair.why: A detective chases a villain who steals characters from books in an alternate England; funny and clever for bookworms.

call of the wild.title: The Call of the Wild
call of the wild.author: Jack London
call of the wild.why: A sled dog turns wild in the Klondike gold rush; short, easy and a favourite classic.

gone girl.title: Gone Girl
gone girl.author: Gillian Flynn
gone girl.why: A wife vanishes and secrets unravel in a twisty thriller with unlikeable characters that readers dissect.

eversion.title: Eversion
eversion.author: Alastair Reynolds
eversion.why: A short reality-bending sci-fi adventure that readers praise as a taste of Reynolds's writing.

hands of the emperor.title: The Hands of the Emperor
hands of the emperor.author: Victoria Goddard
hands of the emperor.why: A slow-building fantasy of a young man's service to a legendary emperor, loved for its heart and humour.

tigana.title: Tigana
tigana.author: Guy Gavriel Kay
tigana.why: A land under a sorcerer's curse, a war of memory; admired for glorious prose even if some plots bother readers.

year of magical thinking.title: Year of Magical Thinking, The
year of magical thinking.author: Joan Didion
year of magical thinking.why: A memoir of the year after her husband's sudden death and the irrational ways grief works.

thief.title: The Thief
thief.author: Megan Whalen Turner
thief.why: Not a clear recommendation of this book.

spinning silver.title: Spinning Silver
spinning silver.author: Naomi Novik
spinning silver.why: A moneylender's daughter in a wintry Eastern European world, a clever fairy-tale retelling with multiple narrators.

do androids dream of electric sheep.title: Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?
do androids dream of electric sheep.author: Philip K. Dick
do androids dream of electric sheep.why: A bounty hunter hunts androids in a ruined world and asks what makes someone human; the book behind Blade Runner.

house of mirth.title: The House of Mirth
house of mirth.author: Edith Wharton
house of mirth.why: A society woman falls out of favour in New York's Gilded Age; tragic and beautifully written.

ninth house.title: Ninth House
ninth house.author: Leigh Bardugo
ninth house.why: Secret societies at Yale deal in dark magic, with a harsh mystery that hooks readers.

just mercy.title: Just Mercy
just mercy.author: Bryan Stevenson
just mercy.why: A lawyer's fight for the wrongly condemned, moving and eye-opening about the US justice system.

chain gang all stars.title: Chain Gang All Stars
chain gang all stars.author: Nana Kwame Adjei-Brenyah
chain gang all stars.why: A near-future where prisoners fight to the death on TV, praised by critics for its sharp edge and urgency.

open.title: Open
open.author: Andre Agassi
open.why: A tennis star's honest, surprising life story, great even for those who do not follow tennis.

all creatures great and small.title: All Creatures Great and Small (All Creatures Great and Small #1-2)
all creatures great and small.author: James Herriot
all creatures great and small.why: A young Yorkshire vet's warm, funny stories about farms and animals; readers re-read it for comfort.

names.title: The Names
names.author: Don DeLillo
names.why: DeLillo's novel of expatriates in Greece and a cult murdering people; admired by readers who love his cool style.

fifth head of cerberus.title: The Fifth Head Of Cerberus
fifth head of cerberus.author: Gene Wolfe
fifth head of cerberus.why: Three linked tales of two planets and identity; a dreamlike science fiction classic.

cows.title: Cows
cows.author: Matthew Stokoe
cows.why: An extremely violent, grim comic horror novel; one reader calls it the most unhinged thing they've read.

where the red fern grows.title: Where the Red Fern Grows
where the red fern grows.author: Wilson Rawls
where the red fern grows.why: A boy and his two hunting dogs in the Ozarks; short and tear-jerking.

orlando.title: Orlando
orlando.author: Virginia Woolf
orlando.why: A poet who changes sex and lives for centuries across English history; playful and demanding.

clockwork orange.title: A Clockwork Orange
clockwork orange.author: Anthony Burgess
clockwork orange.why: A delinquent in a violent future England is reconditioned; short and iconic, in invented slang.

possession.title: Possession
possession.author: A. S. Byatt
possession.why: Two scholars uncover the secret love of Victorian poets in a rich, layered romance and mystery.

steppenwolf.title: Steppenwolf
steppenwolf.author: Herman Hesse
steppenwolf.why: A middle-aged man torn between bourgeois and wild impulses; a great book that some find a difficult read.

endurance shackletons incredible voyage.title: Endurance; Shackleton's incredible voyage
endurance shackletons incredible voyage.author: Alfred Lansing
endurance shackletons incredible voyage.why: The real story of Shackleton's lost ship and crew survival in Antarctica, reads like an adventure novel.

slewfoot.title: Slewfoot
slewfoot.author: Brom
slewfoot.why: A witch-tale about a goat-legged being in colonial Pennsylvania, illustrated; good Halloween reading.

kitchen confidential.title: Kitchen Confidential
kitchen confidential.author: Anthony Bourdain
kitchen confidential.why: A chef's blunt, funny memoir of kitchen life, found witty and warm.

matrix.title: Matrix
matrix.author: Lauren Groff
matrix.why: An abbess in medieval France builds a world of women in a short, magical-realist novel.

caste.title: Caste
caste.author: Isabel Wilkerson
caste.why: A study of America's hidden caste system, urged by readers who want to understand US history and society.

i cheerfully refuse.title: I Cheerfully Refuse
i cheerfully refuse.author: Leif Enger
i cheerfully refuse.why: A family goes on the run in a collapsing near-future America; readers enjoyed it but some withheld judgment.

sun also rises.title: The Sun Also Rises
sun also rises.author: Ernest Hemingway
sun also rises.why: Expatriates in 1920s Paris and Spain travel, drink and aimlessly drift; Hemingway's famous spare style.

underground railroad.title: The Underground Railroad
underground railroad.author: Colson Whitehead
underground railroad.why: A girl's escape from slavery on a literal railroad; an alternative-history novel that won big awards.

remnant population.title: Remnant Population
remnant population.author: Elizabeth Moon
remnant population.why: An old woman is the last of her colony and must meet aliens; praised as outstanding by readers.

cold mountain.title: Cold Mountain
cold mountain.author: Charles Frazier
cold mountain.why: A wounded Confederate soldier walks home across the Civil War South to his love; poetic and slow.

confessions.title: Confessions
confessions.author: Kanae Minato
confessions.why: A teacher's chilling confession opens a revenge story told by several voices; gripping and short.

prodigal summer.title: Prodigal Summer
prodigal summer.author: Barbara Kingsolver
prodigal summer.why: Three lives intertwine in Appalachian nature in Kingsolver's love of the natural world.

greenwood.title: GREENWOOD
greenwood.author: Michael Christie
greenwood.why: A multigenerational tale of trees and a family across time; many readers name it a current favourite.

narrow road to the deep north.title: The Narrow Road to the Deep North
narrow road to the deep north.author: Richard Flanagan
narrow road to the deep north.why: A surgeon on the Burma railway and a love story; harrowing, heartbreaking and prize-winning.

buried giant.title: The Buried Giant
buried giant.author: Kazuo Ishiguro
buried giant.why: An old couple travels a misty post-Arthurian Britain in search of their son; quiet and moving, about memory.

housekeeping.title: Housekeeping
housekeeping.author: Marilynne Robinson
housekeeping.why: Two sisters and their strange aunt in a remote lake town; haunting prose beloved by literary fans.

kushiels dart.title: Kushiel's Dart
kushiels dart.author: Jacqueline Carey
kushiels dart.why: A courtesan spy in a world of intrigue, with deep worldbuilding and heavy themes; the start of a series.

island of sea women.title: The Island of Sea Women
island of sea women.author: Lisa See
island of sea women.why: Two women divers on a Korean island over decades, a gripping portrait of friendship; engrossing.

gunslinger.title: The Gunslinger
gunslinger.author: Stephen King
gunslinger.why: A gunslinger chases the man in black across a desert, opening a strange epic; fans say read the series.

armor.title: Armor
armor.author: John Steakley
armor.why: A reluctant soldier in powered armour fights in endless wars; a gritty military SF recommended by veterans of the genre.
